minutes.headline: Capital committee agreed Marshall Park is next in line if more FY22 capital money appears; threshold change undecided.
minutes.summary: The committee reviewed the FY22 capital plan after revised estimates for the Town Hall and Ritter building projects, and agreed Marshall Park would be next on the ranked list if more money becomes available. It then discussed whether to raise the dollar threshold for capital projects in the selectmen's fiscal policy, without deciding. The next meeting was set for March 2nd.

what_happened.line: The committee agreed that Marshall Park would be next on the ranked FY22 capital list if more money becomes available.
Members reviewed the FY22 capital plan after revised estimates for the Town Hall and Ritter building projects, and checked the Ritter base bid against the spreadsheet.
Leftover money from the underground storage tank project returns to the capital plan only after the project fully closes; paving remains.
Members debated raising the dollar threshold for capital projects in the selectmen's fiscal policy, including a phased increase, and reached no decision.
The next meeting was set for March 2nd to continue the fiscal policy review before the finance committee takes it up in April.

why_it_matters: The ranked capital list decides which town projects are funded first, and the funding sources (free cash, raise and appropriate, stabilization, borrowing) can affect the tax bill and change from year to year.
The fiscal policy threshold decides which purchases count as capital projects and go through this committee, and it is still undecided.
